title: Longest Word in Dictionary
statement: Call a word of `words` *buildable* when every one of its prefixes, from its first letter alone up to the word itself, is also in `words`; in other words, it can be grown from a one-letter word of the list by appending one letter at a time, staying inside the list after every step. Return the buildable word of greatest length. When several buildable words share that length, return the alphabetically smallest of them, and return the empty string `""` when no word is buildable.
constraints: words[i] contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The simple way puts every word in a set and checks all of each word's prefixes, then keeps the best. A trie organises the same check: a word is buildable exactly when every node on its path from the root ends a word. So a depth-first walk that only steps into nodes ending a word reaches precisely the buildable words. Visiting children in alphabetical order meets words in dictionary order, so the first word found at each new record length is the alphabetically smallest of that length.

## Approach

1. Insert every word into a trie of 26-slot nodes, storing the whole word in the node where it ends.
2. Start `best` as `""`.
3. From the root, visit children from `a` to `z`, skipping any child that is missing or does not end a word.
4. When a visited word is strictly longer than `best`, it becomes `best`; then descend into it.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`words = ["w", "wo", "wor", "worl", "world"]` builds a single path `w -> o -> r -> l -> d`, and every node on it ends a word. The walk visits `"w"` (`best = "w"`), then `"wo"`, `"wor"`, `"worl"` and `"world"`, each longer than the last, so `best` ends as `"world"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(L), where L is the total number of letters: each letter is inserted once and each trie node is visited at most once.
- Space: O(26·L) for the trie nodes.

## Pitfalls

- Every prefix must be present, not just the word one letter shorter: in `["a", "abc", "abcd"]` the answer is `"a"`.
- Update only on a strictly longer word; with alphabetical order, the first word of a length is already the smallest.
- Return `""` when no one-letter word exists, since nothing can be built then.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `root` | the empty trie node above all first letters |
| `node` | the trie node being filled or visited |
| `index` | the slot `0` to `25` for a letter |
| `child` | one child slot of `node` |
| `best` | the longest buildable word found so far |

narration.2: The root stands for the empty prefix and has 26 child slots, one per letter.
narration.3: Insert every word into the trie.
narration.5: Walk the word letter by letter.
narration.6: Turn the letter into a slot number from 0 to 25.
narration.7: Create the child node if this prefix has not been seen yet.
narration.10: Step down to the node for the prefix so far.
narration.12: Mark the last node with the whole word it ends.
narration.15: No word found yet, so the answer starts empty.
narration.17: Visit the children in alphabetical order.
narration.18: Skip a missing child or one that does not end a word: nothing below it is buildable.
narration.21: A strictly longer buildable word beats the best; alphabetical order already breaks ties.
narration.22: Remember it as the new best.
narration.24: Keep extending this buildable word one letter at a time.
narration.27: Start the walk at the root.
narration.28: Return the longest, alphabetically smallest buildable word.
